## Installation

Install the published package from PyPI (`aspose-3d-foss`, version 26.1.0):

```bash
python3 -m pip install aspose-3d-foss
```

To work from the latest source checkout instead, install it in editable mode:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/aspose-3d-foss/Aspose.3D-FOSS-for-Python.git
cd Aspose.3D-FOSS-for-Python
python3 -m pip install -e .
```

Verify the install:

```bash
python3 -c "from aspose.threed import Scene; print('Aspose.3D FOSS OK')"
```

The package supports Python 3.7, 3.8, 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12 on Windows, macOS, and Linux,
with no native dependencies.

## Installation

Aspose.Cells FOSS for Rust is not yet published to [crates.io](https://crates.io/) (see
[Scope and Limitations](#scope-and-limitations)). Once the repository is live at its real
GitHub location, add it as a Git dependency in `Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[dependencies]
aspose-cells-foss-rust = { git = "https://github.com/aspose-cells-foss/Aspose.Cells-FOSS-for-Rust" }
```

For local development against a cloned copy, use a path dependency instead:

```toml
[dependencies]
aspose-cells-foss-rust = { path = "../Aspose.Cells-FOSS-for-Rust" }
```

The package name is `aspose-cells-foss-rust`; the library is imported as
`aspose_cells_foss_rust`. Requires a recent stable Rust toolchain (2021 edition or later).
No proprietary Aspose runtime and no Microsoft Office installation is required.

To build the library directly from a clone:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/aspose-cells-foss/Aspose.Cells-FOSS-for-Rust.git
cd Aspose.Cells-FOSS-for-Rust
cargo build
```

# Aspose.Imaging FOSS for .NET [![CI](https://github.com/aspose-imaging-foss/Aspose.Imaging-FOSS-for-.NET/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/aspose-imaging-foss/Aspose.Imaging-FOSS-for-.NET/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Contributors](https://img.shields.io/github/contributors/aspose-imaging-foss/Aspose.Imaging-FOSS-for-.NET.svg)](https://github.com/aspose-imaging-foss/Aspose.Imaging-FOSS-for-.NET/graphs/contributors) [![Aspose.Imaging FOSS for .NET](https://products.aspose.org/media/imaging/net/banner-readme.png)](https://products.aspose.org/imaging/net/) Aspose.Imaging FOSS for .NET is a free, open-source .NET library — an Aspose.Imaging alternative that does zero-dependency image format detection and header probing. `ImageProbe` identifies a file's format and reads its basic properties — dimensions, bit depth, and frame count — directly from the file header, so you know what a file is and how big it is, fast, without pulling in a full imaging stack to decode a single pixel. It has no NuGet dependencies and targets `netstandard2.0` and `net8.0`. ## Navigation - [At a Glance](#at-a-glance) - [Key Capabilities](#key-capabilities) - [Installation](#installation) - [Dependencies](#dependencies) - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Additional Examples](#additional-examples) - [API Reference](#api-reference) - [Documentation & Resources](#documentation--resources) - [Scope and Limitations](#scope-and-limitations) - [Development and Testing](#development-and-testing) - [License](#license) ## At a Glance ```mermaid %%{init: {"flowchart": {"useMaxWidth": true}}}%% flowchart TD subgraph StartingPoints["Starting Points"] direction TB i1["Image files
(PNG, JPEG,
GIF, BMP)"] i2["Image files
(ICO, TIFF,
WEBP)"] i3["Image files
(PSD, EMF,
WMF)"] i4["Image files
(DICOM, DJVU,
AVIF, HEIC)"] end PRODUCT["Aspose.Imaging FOSS for .NET"] subgraph Capabilities["Core Capabilities"] direction TB c1["Format detection,
tolerant of
bad input"] c2["Dimension,
bit-depth,
frame count"] c3["Sync/async
probing"] end subgraph Outputs["Outputs"] direction TB o1["Images
(ImageFormat,
ImageInfo)"] end StartingPoints --> PRODUCT --> Capabilities --> Outputs ``` ## Key Capabilities - Detects 14 image formats as a free, open source Aspose.Imaging alternative to a full decode pipeline — `ImageProbe.DetectFormat()` reads only the file's signature bytes and returns an `ImageFormat` value, so identifying a file never requires pulling in a full imaging stack. - `ImageProbe.Probe()` reads a format's real header fields directly into an `ImageInfo` — width, height, bit depth, and frame count — for PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, WEBP (lossy, lossless, and extended), ICO, TIFF, PSD, EMF, WMF, DICOM, DJVU, AVIF, and HEIC/HEIF, as a free open source .NET image manipulation API with no decode step. - Counts real multi-frame and multi-page content where the container format actually carries it: GIF walks its image-descriptor blocks, ICO its directory entries, TIFF its IFD chain, and a bundled multi-page DJVU (DJVM) its `FORM:DJVU` page components — not the DIRM file count, which also includes shared dictionaries and thumbnails. - DICOM parsing covers Implicit VR Little Endian and Explicit VR Little/Big Endian transfer syntaxes — including the common compressed ones, whose non-pixel elements are encoded Explicit VR Little Endian — and reads `Rows`/`Columns`/`BitsAllocated` directly from the data set, stopping rather than guessing if it reaches a sequence or encapsulated pixel data element with an undefined length first. - AVIF and HEIC/HEIF dimensions come from the primary image's `ispe` (image spatial extent) property: `pitm` names the primary item and `ipma` links it to its `ipco` properties, so grid images (such as iPhone photos) report the full canvas rather than a tile. Without those associations the largest `ispe` is used. AVIF is detected by an `avif`/`avis` major brand, or by a compatible `avif`/`avis` brand under a generic major brand such as `mif1`; HEIC/HEIF by `heic`, `heix`, `hevc`, `hevx`, `heim`, `heis`, `hevm`, `hevs`, or `mif1`/`mif2` without AVIF. - Every number in an `ImageInfo` is either positive or `null`: zero, negative, or out-of-range header fields are reported as unknown instead of being passed through. - `Probe()` never throws on a signature match it can't fully parse — malformed or truncated input comes back as an `ImageInfo` with only `Format` set, never an exception, so a probing pipeline can run unattended over untrusted input. - Both synchronous and async entry points exist for the same operation — `ProbeFile()`/`ProbeFileAsync()` and `Probe()`/`ProbeAsync()` — so a probe can run on an ASP.NET request thread without blocking it. Most .NET image libraries make you fully decode an image just to answer "is this a JPEG, and how big is it?". `ImageSharp.Image.Identify` covers common raster formats well, but nothing else in the .NET FOSS ecosystem does the same for PSD, EMF/WMF, or DICOM — this library covers that full range in one place. | Format | Detect | Width / Height | Bit depth | Frame count | |--------|:------:|:---------------:|:---------:|:-----------:| | PNG | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | — | | JPEG | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | — | | GIF | ✅ | ✅ | — | ✅ | | BMP | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | — | | WEBP (lossy / lossless / extended) | ✅ | ✅ | — | — | | ICO | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | TIFF | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | PSD | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | — | | EMF | ✅ | ✅ (from bounds) | — | — | | WMF (placeable) | ✅ | ✅ (assumes 96 DPI) | — | — | | DICOM | ✅ | ✅ (Rows/Columns) | ✅ (BitsAllocated) | — | | DJVU (single-page / multi-page DJVM) | ✅ | ✅ | — | ✅ | | AVIF (still / animated) | ✅ | ✅ | — | — | | HEIC / HEIF | ✅ | ✅ | — | — | Frame count is marked ✅ only where the container format genuinely records more than one frame or page (GIF, ICO, TIFF, and multi-page DJVU); every other format's `FrameCount` comes back as a fixed `1` on a successful parse, which this table does not count as a real frame count. ## Installation Build and install from a clone of the repository: ```bash git clone https://github.com/aspose-imaging-foss/Aspose.Imaging-FOSS-for-.NET.git cd Aspose.Imaging-FOSS-for-.NET dotnet build src/Aspose.Imaging.Foss/Aspose.Imaging.Foss.csproj -c Release ``` Reference the built assembly from another project, or add the project directly: ```xml ``` The library multi-targets `netstandard2.0` and `net8.0` — see [Dependencies](#dependencies) below for the full required, native, and development-only breakdown. ## Dependencies ### Required Package Dependencies No required third-party package dependencies. The library builds from `src/Aspose.Imaging.Foss/Aspose.Imaging.Foss.csproj`, which declares zero `` entries — every format's header parsing is implemented natively within the library. ### Native and System Requirements - Targets `netstandard2.0` and `net8.0` (see [Installation](#installation)). ### Development Dependencies - `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` 17.12.0, `xunit` 2.9.2, and `xunit.runner.visualstudio` 2.8.2 — the xUnit test host and adapter used only by the test project. - `coverlet.collector` 6.0.2 — code-coverage collection for the test suite. None of these are referenced by the main library project; they apply only to `tests/Aspose.Imaging.Foss.Tests/Aspose.Imaging.Foss.Tests.csproj` and are never shipped with the library. ## Quick Start ```csharp using Aspose.Imaging.Foss; // From a file path var info = ImageProbe.ProbeFile("photo.jpg"); Console.WriteLine($"{info.Format}: {info.Width}x{info.Height}, {info.BitDepth}-bit"); // From a stream (seekable or not) or a byte array var format = ImageProbe.DetectFormat(bytes); var info2 = ImageProbe.Probe(stream); ``` `Probe` never throws on malformed or truncated input — if a file matches a format's signature but its header can't be fully parsed, you get back an `ImageInfo` with just the `Format` set rather than an exception. ## Additional Examples
View Additional Examples ### Probe a File Asynchronously `ProbeFileAsync()` and `ProbeAsync()` mirror their synchronous counterparts for use on a thread that shouldn't block on I/O, such as an ASP.NET request handler: ```csharp using Aspose.Imaging.Foss; var info = await ImageProbe.ProbeFileAsync("upload.png", cancellationToken); Console.WriteLine($"{info.Format}: {info.Width}x{info.Height}"); ``` ### Count Frames in a Multi-Frame GIF or a Multi-Page DJVU `FrameCount` is only populated with a real count for formats whose container actually records one — an animated GIF's image-descriptor blocks, or the page components of a bundled multi-page DJVU (DJVM) document: ```csharp using Aspose.Imaging.Foss; var info = ImageProbe.ProbeFile("animation.gif"); Console.WriteLine($"{info.Format}: {info.FrameCount} frame(s)"); ``` ### Detect a Format From an Unseekable Stream `DetectFormat` and `Probe` both buffer a non-seekable stream internally, so detection works the same way over a network or compressed stream as it does over a file: ```csharp using Aspose.Imaging.Foss; using var networkStream = GetUploadStream(); // CanSeek == false var format = ImageProbe.DetectFormat(networkStream); ```
## API Reference `ImageProbe` is the library's single entry point; it returns an `ImageFormat` value and an `ImageInfo` record for every supported format.
View the Full API Surface #### Detailed Member Reference - `ImageFormat` — enum of the 14 detectable formats, plus `Unknown` for anything unmatched. - `ImageInfo` — immutable result of a probe: `Format`, and the nullable `Width`, `Height`, `BitDepth`, and `FrameCount` the format's header actually carried. - `ImageProbe` — static entry point: `DetectFormat`, `Probe`, `ProbeFile`, `ProbeAsync`, and `ProbeFileAsync`. - `ImageProbe.DetectFormat(Stream stream) -> ImageFormat` / `DetectFormat(byte[] data) -> ImageFormat` — signature-only match, no dimension parsing. - `ImageProbe.Probe(Stream stream) -> ImageInfo` / `Probe(byte[] data) -> ImageInfo` / `Probe(FileInfo file) -> ImageInfo` — full header parse for whichever format's signature matches. - `ImageProbe.ProbeFile(string path) -> ImageInfo` — opens the file and calls `Probe`. - `ImageProbe.ProbeAsync(Stream stream, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) -> Task` / `ProbeFileAsync(string path, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) -> Task` — async counterparts of `Probe`/`ProbeFile`. - `ImageInfo(ImageFormat format, int? width = null, int? height = null, int? bitDepth = null, int? frameCount = null)` — the only public constructor; every field besides `Format` is nullable because not every format's header carries all four.
## Documentation & Resources - **[Getting started guide](https://docs.aspose.org/imaging/net/)** — installation and a first probe, walked through step by step. - **[How-to guides & FAQ](https://kb.aspose.org/imaging/net/)** — task-focused answers for common format-detection questions. - **[Full API reference](https://reference.aspose.org/imaging/net/)** — the complete browsable reference for `ImageFormat`, `ImageInfo`, and `ImageProbe`. - Found a bug or have a feature request? [Open an issue](https://github.com/aspose-imaging-foss/Aspose.Imaging-FOSS-for-.NET/issues) on GitHub. ## Scope and Limitations - **Detection and metadata only.** `ImageProbe` identifies a format and reads its header fields; it never decodes pixel data, so there is no rendering, editing, or format-conversion capability anywhere in the library. - **Frame count reflects only what the container itself records.** It is a real, computed count for GIF, ICO, TIFF, and bundled multi-page DJVU (DJVM); every other supported format reports a fixed `1` for a successfully parsed header, since none of their headers carry a genuine frame or page count. An indirect (multi-file) DJVM document, or a truncated bundled one, reports `FrameCount` as `null`, since its pages can't all be seen from the one file. - **Non-placeable WMF is detected but not dimensioned.** The classic (non-placeable) WMF header carries no bounding rectangle, so `Probe` returns a format-only `ImageInfo` for it; only the placeable WMF header (identified by its own magic number) yields `Width`/`Height`. Placeable-WMF dimensions assume a conventional 96 DPI target, since the header only stores units-per-inch bounds. - **DICOM parsing stops at the first undefined-length element.** A sequence or encapsulated pixel-data element with an undefined length ends the walk rather than being parsed, since `Rows`/`Columns`/`BitsAllocated` always precede such elements in a conformant file. - **CDR support is planned but not yet implemented** — no `CdrFormatHandler` exists in the current source tree. These limitations apply only to Aspose.Imaging FOSS — they don't carry over to [Aspose.Imaging for .NET — Enterprise Edition](https://products.aspose.com/imaging/net/), which adds full decoding, editing, rendering, and conversion across a much broader format range. ## Development and Testing Run the test suite from the repository root: ```bash dotnet test tests/Aspose.Imaging.Foss.Tests/Aspose.Imaging.Foss.Tests.csproj ``` The test project targets `net9.0` and references the library via a plain `ProjectReference` — no packaged dependency is required to build or test the library itself. A tagged `v..` push runs [`.github/workflows/release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml), which builds and publishes the package. Adding a new format means implementing `IFormatHandler` (signature match + header parse) under `src/Aspose.Imaging.Foss/Formats` and registering it in `ImageProbe`. Pull requests for new formats or wider tag/chunk coverage on existing ones are welcome. ## License This project is licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE). The MIT License permits use, copying, modification, distribution, sublicensing, and commercial use, provided its copyright and permission notice are retained. The software is provided without warranty.

## Installation

Install the package from PyPI:

```bash
pip install aspose-page-foss
```

To build and verify a wheel from a clone of the repository instead, install `uv`, `setuptools`,
and `wheel`, then run:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/aspose-page-foss/Aspose.Page-FOSS-for-Python.git
cd Aspose.Page-FOSS-for-Python
python package.py build
python package.py verify
```

The wheel version comes from `local/Version.txt`. `verify` installs it with all dependencies
in `.package-venv` and tests PS/XPS to PDF/PNG conversion. To upload the built wheel, use
`python package.py publish-test` for TestPyPI or `python package.py publish` for PyPI; these
commands read credentials from the matching files in `local/`.

The library targets Python 3.10+ (`pyproject.toml`'s `requires-python = ">=3.10"`). See
[Dependencies](#dependencies) below for the full required/optional/native breakdown.

pdf-cpp.readme_installation:
## Installation

This library builds as a static library you link into your project. Either way, include the whole
public API through the single-entry header, or include individual headers from `aspose/pdf/`:

```cpp
#include <aspose.pdf.foss.hpp>
```

### Visual Studio (NuGet)

Install the [`Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS) package
into a C++ project (`Install-Package Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS`). It ships static libraries for x64,
x86, and ARM64 in Release and Debug. It adds the include path, links the matching library, and
raises the project to C++20.

### From a Release Archive

Each [GitHub release](https://github.com/aspose-pdf-foss/Aspose.PDF-FOSS-for-Cpp/releases) ships
prebuilt archives for Linux x64 (GCC 13) and Windows x64 (MSVC, with Release and Debug libraries).
Each archive contains the public headers, the static library, and a CMake package. Extract it and
point `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` at the extracted folder:

```cmake
find_package(aspose_pdf_foss 1.0 CONFIG REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(your_app PRIVATE aspose_pdf_foss::aspose_pdf_foss)
```

The same package is produced by `cmake --install build --prefix <dir>` from a source build.

### As a CMake Subdirectory

```cmake
add_subdirectory(aspose.pdf-foss-for-cpp)
target_link_libraries(your_app PRIVATE aspose_pdf_foss::aspose_pdf_foss)
```

Both forms of the target make your code compile as C++20.

### Requirements

- A C++20 compiler (clang 16+, gcc 13+, or MSVC 2022 17.5+)
- CMake 3.20 or later
- Python 3, build-time only — a generator step embeds the bundled font outlines into a generated
  source file

**Runtime dependencies: none.** The test suite alone fetches
[GoogleTest](https://github.com/google/googletest) v1.14.0 via CMake `FetchContent` at configure
time; it is not needed to build or consume the library itself.

### Build From Source

```bash
cmake -S . -B build
cmake --build build
```

The static library lands at `build/libaspose_pdf_foss.a` (or `aspose_pdf_foss.lib` on MSVC), built
out-of-source under `build/`. For a release build, pass `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release` to the
configure step. `CMakePresets.json` also carries host-conditional Windows-MSVC presets — e.g.
`cmake --preset windows-msvc-debug`.
